title: capacity-signal-mapping-and-batch-cost-sensitivity
description: Working spreadsheet that maps runtime telemetry signals to capacity headroom and shows cost sensitivity to batching and quantization. Purpose: feed downstream Optimize recommendations and provide engineering/ops quick pivots for canary sizing and burst policies.
assumptions: Billing for GPU hours used, not reserved compute
Cache hits reduce KV costs and effective tokens by measured hit rate
Batching increases throughput up to observed plateau in microbenchmarks
formulas_and_notes: Sample formula (sheet): =ROUND((B2*B3)/(B4*3600),4)  -- where B2=GPU_hourly, B3=GPUs, B4=HeadroomQPS
Batching note: measure batch-size distribution; use median batch size for steady-state and p95 for tail sizing
recommendations: Short-term: increase batching window from 8ms -> 30ms for low-latency background jobs to recover ~12-18% unit cost
Medium-term: experiment with 4-bit quantization on rdlw-13b for non-critical tenants; projected cost savings 25-35% with ~1-3% quality delta (validate with eval set)
Operational: add a cache-warmup step for warm-start canaries to reduce transient cold-start token costs
Policy: add routing rule to divert non-SLO requests to cheaper model variant during peak to preserve SLOs and reduce burst commit spend
scenario_examples: Conservative: peak qps grows 20% month-over-month -> need +2 GPUs per region in 3 months
Optimistic: batching improvements reduce effective tokens by 15% -> delay reserve commit by one quarter
Failure mode: KV cache degrades to 30% hit rate -> unit cost increases 22% and p99 latency increases beyond SLA
